title: Morning Robotics Scan
report:
## Fortescue KUKA Welding Robots for 6 MW Charger Cables

### The Breakthrough
Fortescue repurposes high‑torque KUKA automotive‑line welding robots to precisely maneuver multi‑ton, liquid‑cooled charging cables, enabling a 3.2 MWh battery charge in about 30 minutes—a controlled 6 MW power transfer to its massive electric haul truck.

### The Caveats
The claim rests only on a demo video with no quantitative performance numbers, safety analysis, or comparison to existing charging‑connection methods.

## China’s Massive Street Delivery Robot Deployment

### The Breakthrough
City‑level regulatory sandboxes let autonomous cargo vehicles share public roads for 24‑hour operation; Neolix raised $400 M to expand beyond 30,000 units and Meituan reports over 5.5 M outdoor deliveries slated by end‑2025.

### The Caveats
The reported large‑scale deployment is based solely on company announcements and media reports, lacking independent verification of performance, safety, or impact.

## OpenTac 3D Tactile Skin Ecosystem

### The Breakthrough
OpenTac provides a resistive tactile skin with a CAD tool that auto‑generates fabrication files; partial readouts achieve 1 kHz operation, a 19.2× speedup over full‑array scans on a 1024‑taxel array, demonstrated on four robot platforms.

### The Caveats
The paper offers no comparison to existing tactile sensors, leaving its claimed speed and performance advantages unsubstantiated.

## Swarming Robo‑Dogs Hacchan for Bear Patrol

### The Breakthrough
Hacchan combines onboard vision, a speaker for deterrent barks, and wireless communication to form a self‑organizing swarm that logs bear sightings and builds a behavior database for optimized patrols.

### The Caveats
The autonomous bear‑deterrence capability has never been tested in real conditions, with no field‑trial data to confirm effectiveness.

## WarpWeaver Decentralized Multi‑Robot Planner

### The Breakthrough
WarpWeaver extends dispersive‑tree search with local constraints and decentralized column‑generation negotiation, reducing total travel time by up to 22% versus centralized offline planners and 37% versus a decentralized baseline; demonstrated on six robots.

### The Caveats
The method is validated only on a six‑robot platform, leaving scalability to larger teams untested.

## DiffDreamer Agile Quadrotor Control

### The Breakthrough
DiffDreamer couples a latent‑space world model with a differentiable physics simulator, enabling joint gradient‑based actor optimization that converges faster and achieves higher success rates on aggressive tracking and gate‑racing tasks.

### The Caveats
Performance gains are shown only in simulation and a single proof‑of‑concept flight, with no broader real‑world validation.

## Humanoid Mobility via Attention‑Based Contact Planning

### The Breakthrough
A self‑supervised attention‑based contact planner predicts future foot contacts, feeding a contact‑conditioned tracker that generates whole‑body motions from onboard observations without reference trajectories.

### The Caveats
The paper provides no evaluation details or baseline comparisons, so the claimed versatile mobility remains unverified.

## Survey of Miniaturized Military Robots

### The Breakthrough
The survey catalogues ultra‑small platforms—from 80‑100 mg RoboBee to >100‑drone PERDIX swarms—highlighting AI‑driven distributed control, compact power electronics, and high‑frequency actuation that enable confined‑space navigation and swarm coordination.

### The Caveats
Claims rest solely on cited specifications, with no empirical field tests or benchmark comparisons to validate performance.

## Tingde Liu’s Embodied AI Research Notes Site

### The Breakthrough
A Jekyll‑powered website bundles multilingual research summaries, automated translation validation scripts, and a CI pipeline that lints, tests, and builds on every push, offering reusable SCSS styling and modular content layout.

### The Caveats
The site’s usefulness is never empirically validated; no user studies confirm its value as a comprehensive knowledge base.

### Priority
Fortescue’s demonstration of KUKA welding robots handling massive 6 MW charging cables shows a concrete path to automating hazardous heavy‑duty tasks in mining, making it the most actionable story today.

### One action
Track forthcoming safety and performance data from Fortescue’s demo and evaluate KUKA robot integration for similar high‑torque, heavy‑payload applications.
